title.full: ASEAN Green Future Project Phase 2.2 Report, Optimization of Laos's Power Generation Sector

publisher.full: Sustainable Development Solutions Network and ClimateWorks Centre

name.full: Optimized More Ambitious Policy Scenario LA

description: Pathway balancing high renewables uptake with minimal coal use and reduced hydropower investment.
pathwayDescription:
The Optimized More Ambitious Policy (OMAP) scenario models Laos’s power and energy systems using the Low Emissions Analysis Platform (LEAP) under the ASEAN Green Future (AGF) project. It builds on the More Ambitious Policy (MAP) scenario by applying a least-cost optimization approach, seeking the lowest-cost pathway to reach near-zero emissions in Laos’s power sector and economy-wide. The resulting trajectory differs from MAP in several ways. Unlike in MAP, the power sector does not reach true-zero emissions in OMAP, with residual emissions from biomass totaling 22,960 metric tons, less than 1% of 2020 levels. 

Additionally, this pathway meets demand with less total capacity (25.6 GW in 2050, versus 40.9 GW in the More Ambitious Policy scenario), and it does so using renewables, which are cheaper than hydro (hydropower peaks at 10 GW in 2050, compared to 26 GW in the More Ambitious Policy scenario). As a result, the total power system costs in OMAP are lower than in both the MAP pathway and the Existing Policy pathway, indicating that the large-scale investments in the OMAP pathway significantly improve future cost-competitiveness.

coreDrivers.policies: Hydro additions are aligned with the NDC until 2030, but doesn't continue after 2030. As coal power is phased out in 2040 and needs to be replaced, additional wind and solar are added to the pathway.
coreDrivers.emissionsTargets: Near-zero 2050 and coal phase-out by 2040 constrain the pathway.
coreDrivers.technologyCosts: Least-cost optimization determines dispatch and generation mix.
coreDrivers.macroeconomicDrivers: SSP2 GDP, medium population growth extracted from World Bank and some ambitous electrification assumptions in housings and transportation drive electricity demand.

dependencies.dependency_description: Hydro additions are aligned with the NDC until 2030, but doesn't continue after 2030. As coal power is phased out in 2040 and needs to be replaced, additional wind and solar are added to the pathway.
The pathway suggests impementing more supportive and clearer rules for clean-energy investment and regional energy trading would be conducive to achieving its modeled outcomes.

OMAP used a Least Cost approach, and total investment is then less important than in MAP for the same level of ambition. Cross-border electricity trade with Thailand is economically important, but the pathway does not provide forward-looking trade volumes or prices that determine the OMAP outcome.

OMAP deals with demand-side behavior through much stronger exogenous electrification assumptions, including 50% passenger EV penetration in 2030 and 100% in 2050 and substantially higher electric-truck uptake. This raises electricity demand, but consumer preferences itself is not modeled endogenously.

OMAP uses a different optimized mix with less hydropower and more wind and solar but likewise provides no quantified transmission expansion. Grid integration is therefore an implementation dependency that is not explicitly resolved in the pathway.
This scenario does't reach hydro maximum potential by 2050. Solar and Wind compensates the lack in hydro generation versus other scenarios.

Seasonal water availability affects hydropower adequacy in the dry season. Laos power grid is already dependant on Thailand during that period. OMAP is less reliant on hydro power capacity, but this reduction is for cost-optimization reasons and not due to environmental or ecosystem constraints.
The electrical system requires substantial human resources for its operation. This is not measured in this analysis.
